figures.caption: 圖一：拉麵店的單人座位
figures.description: 晚上七點的拉麵店裡，一排吧檯座位用木製隔板一格一格隔開，四名客人各自坐在自己的小隔間裡低頭吃拉麵，彼此看不到對方的臉；其中一名男客人一邊吃麵一邊看手機。每個座位前方掛著布簾，布簾下只看得到廚師的一雙手正遞出一碗拉麵。牆上的牌子寫著「單人座位」「歡迎一個人來用餐」。

questions.stem: 提示：近年來，越來越多人選擇一個人上餐廳吃飯，有些餐廳也特別設計了單人座位；但也有不少人仍喜歡和家人朋友圍桌共餐。請仔細觀察下面兩張圖，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段比較圖一與圖二兩種用餐情境的不同；第二段說明你認為越來越多人選擇一個人吃飯的原因，評估這個現象對個人或人際關係的影響，並提出你在日常生活中兼顧獨自用餐與和他人共餐的具體做法。

1.explanation_zh: 這一題第一段比較兩種用餐情境；第二段有三項任務：一個人吃飯越來越普遍的原因、對個人或人際關係的影響、自己兼顧兩種用餐方式的做法。第一段的比較點可以從圖中找：木製隔板與單人座位、低頭看手機與聊天大笑、一個人吃麵與一家八口分享多道菜。第二段任務多，要分配篇幅：原因寫一兩個具體的，影響最好兼顧正反兩面，做法要具體（例如哪幾天和家人一起吃），不要只寫「我會平衡」。
evidence: 比較圖一與圖二兩種用餐情境的不同
說明你認為越來越多人選擇一個人吃飯的原因
評估這個現象對個人或人際關係的影響
提出你在日常生活中兼顧獨自用餐與和他人共餐的具體做法
1.strategy_zh: 原因可以從「作息與居住方式」和「想要獨處」兩個角度寫；影響先肯定自由與休息，再寫長期缺少共餐對關係的影響；最後用自己的經驗帶出做法，讓做法有理由。
hints: 第一段：從座位設計、互動、氣氛三點對照兩張圖
第二段前半：寫一兩個具體原因，再評估對個人與人際關係的正反影響
第二段後半：用自己的經驗帶出兼顧兩邊的具體安排，最後寫出見解

moves.zh: 比較圖一與圖二兩種用餐情境的不同
說明你認為越來越多人選擇一個人吃飯的原因
評估這個現象對個人或人際關係的影響
提出你在日常生活中兼顧獨自用餐與和他人共餐的具體做法

content.focus_zh: 第一段要用圖中細節比較兩種用餐情境（座位設計、人與人的互動、氣氛）；第二段要說明一個人吃飯越來越普遍的原因，評估對個人或人際關係的影響（最好兼顧正反兩面），並提出自己兼顧獨自用餐與共餐的具體做法。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。
漏掉題目的主要要求或主旨模糊，多數句子空泛、重複或偏離題目。
空白、離題、只抄題目，或內容少到無法判斷要說什麼。

organization.focus_zh: 第一段以對照方式比較兩張圖並歸納；第二段任務多，要依「原因、影響、自己的做法」推進，用轉承語標出每一步，結尾提出見解。

bands.descriptor_zh: 兩段分工清楚，各有主題句；句與句、段與段的銜接自然，轉承語用得恰當，篇幅分配合理。
段落大致分明，但有的地方跳接或重複，轉承語偏少或用得生硬。
重點排列混亂，前後句常接不起來，讀者不容易跟上。
看不出段落與順序，句子彼此無關。

grammar.focus_zh: 描述圖片用現在式或現在進行式；說明原因與影響可用 because、so、if 條件句與 may、might；寫自己的做法可用現在完成式（have followed）與頻率副詞。

bands.descriptor_zh: 句子幾乎沒有文法、標點錯誤，能交替使用簡單句、複句與不同的句首。
偶有時態、單複數或標點錯誤，但讀得懂意思；句型變化有限。
錯誤多到常讓人誤解意思，句子結構常不完整。
幾乎沒有正確的句子，無法理解。

vocabulary.focus_zh: 用餐相關字詞要精確（solo dining、booth、counter、share dishes、company、solitude），避免一直重複 eat、alone、family。

bands.descriptor_zh: 用字精準、貼切，搭配自然，少有重複；拼字與大小寫幾乎全對。
字彙範圍偏窄、常重複同幾個字，偶有用字不當或拼錯，但不妨礙理解。
用錯字或拼錯字很多，常讓人看不懂。
幾乎每個字都用錯或拼錯，無法理解。

rubric.deductions_zh: 字數明顯不足（少於 100 個單詞）或沒有分成兩段，各扣總分 1 分；兩種情形同時發生只扣 1 分。離題或空白以 0 分計。

checklist_zh: 第一段有沒有用座位設計、互動、氣氛等細節比較兩張圖，而且細節和圖一致
第二段的原因是否具體（例如作息、居住方式、想要獨處），而不是只說「大家很忙」
影響是否兼顧個人與人際關係、正面與負面
自己的做法是否具體（什麼時候一個人吃、什麼時候和家人朋友吃），並和前面的評估連得起來；結尾是否提出見解

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The two pictures show two very different ways of eating out. In Picture 1, four customers are eating ramen alone at a counter. Each of them sits in a small booth with wooden walls on both sides, so they cannot see one another's faces. One man is even looking at his phone while he eats. In Picture 2, however, a big family of eight is sharing many dishes at a round table. The grandparents sit in the middle, a little boy is putting food into his grandmother's bowl, and everyone is talking and laughing. There is also a birthday cake on the table.
I think more people choose to eat alone for two reasons. First, many people are busy with work or school, so eating alone saves time. Second, some people enjoy a quiet meal after spending the whole day with others. Eating alone gives people freedom, but if they always eat alone, they may feel lonely and talk less with their families. When I was preparing for an important exam last year, I often ate dinner by myself at a noodle shop near my cram school. It was convenient, but I missed chatting with my parents. Now I follow a simple plan. On weekdays, I sometimes eat alone when I am in a hurry, but I always have dinner with my family on weekends. In this way, I can enjoy both my own time and my family's company.

paragraphs.function_zh: 比較兩張圖：圖一拉麵店的單人隔間，客人各自吃麵；圖二一家八口圍著圓桌分享菜餚、聊天大笑
paragraphs.topic_sentence: The two pictures show two very different ways of eating out.

paragraphs.function_zh: 原因＋評估＋提出方案：用 First、Second 寫兩個原因，評估自由與孤單兩面，用自己考試前獨自吃飯的經驗帶出平日與週末的安排
paragraphs.topic_sentence: I think more people choose to eat alone for two reasons.

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
The two pictures capture opposite ends of how people share, or do not share, a meal. In Picture 1, four diners sit side by side at a ramen counter, yet each one is sealed off in a narrow booth by wooden panels, so no one can see a neighbor's face. A curtain hangs in front of every seat, and all that can be seen of the cook is a pair of hands passing out a bowl. A sign on the wall makes the message clear: solo customers are welcome. One diner even scrolls through his phone between bites. Picture 2 could hardly be more different. Three generations of a family gather around a large round table covered with dishes, with the grandparents seated at the center and a little boy placing food in his grandmother's bowl, while a birthday cake sits on the table. Whereas the ramen shop is designed to reduce social contact, the family restaurant is designed to encourage it.
Several forces lie behind the rise of solo dining. Long working hours and crowded schedules leave many people with irregular mealtimes, and more young adults now live alone in cities, far from their families. For some, a meal alone is also a welcome break from constant social demands, especially after a day full of meetings and group chats. On a personal level, this trend can be healthy: eating alone gives people the freedom to decide what, when, and how quickly to eat, and it can offer a few minutes of genuine rest. However, if solo meals become the norm rather than a choice, relationships may suffer, because shared meals are where families catch up, settle small conflicts, and pass on traditions. During my exam year, I ate most dinners alone at a convenience store, and I gradually realized that I no longer knew what was happening in my younger brother's life. Since then, I have followed a simple rule. On busy days, I eat alone whenever I need quiet time, but every Wednesday and Sunday evening, we all turn off our phones and eat together as a family. Restaurants could support a similar balance by offering both private counters and shared tables, so that customers can choose solitude or company depending on the day. In the end, eating alone is not a problem in itself; it becomes one only when people no longer have anyone to eat with.

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 第一段用隔板、布簾、夾菜、生日蛋糕等細節比較兩張圖並歸納設計目的；第二段有三個具體原因、對個人與人際關係的正反影響、親身經驗、自己的用餐規則，並延伸到餐廳的設計，結尾提出見解（內容 5）；依原因、影響、做法推進，轉承語功能多樣（組織 5）；分詞片語、名詞子句、with 句型、現在完成式等句型多變且正確（文法句構 5）；用字精準（solitude、irregular、genuine），仍以常用字為主（字彙拼字 4）。總分 19，屬頂標版。

steady.comment_zh: 四項要求都有回應：第一段比較圖一四名客人在木隔板的小隔間各自吃拉麵、一人看手機，和圖二一家八口圍圓桌分菜、小男孩替奶奶夾菜、有生日蛋糕；第二段用 First、Second 列出兩個原因（忙碌省時、想安靜），評估獨自用餐帶來自由但可能孤單、少與家人交談，以考試期間獨自在麵店吃晚餐的經驗佐證，最後說明平日趕時間獨自吃、週末一定和家人吃飯的做法。缺點是第一段沒有歸納兩種情境的根本差異，影響的分析偏短；eat、alone 重複很多。未見文法、用字或標點錯誤。

top.comment_zh: 第一段細節完整（隔板隔開的座位、布簾下只見廚師的手、歡迎單人用餐的牌子、滑手機的客人；三代同堂、轉盤上的菜、替奶奶夾菜、生日蛋糕），並以 Whereas 歸納「減少接觸 vs. 鼓勵接觸」的設計差異；第二段依原因（工時長、作息不規律、年輕人獨居、想喘口氣）、影響（正面是自由與休息，負面是人際關係受損）、自己的做法（考試那年不了解弟弟近況後，每週三、日晚上全家關手機一起吃飯）推進，並延伸到餐廳可同時提供單人座與共桌，結尾見解有力。句構多變、用字精準（sealed off、solo dining、the norm rather than a choice、solitude or company）。未見錯誤；篇幅偏長，但不影響分數。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段把兩張圖分別描述並用 however 對照，缺少歸納差異的句子；第二段依原因、影響、做法推進，有備考時獨自吃飯的經驗與平日／週末分開的做法。理由偏籠統，eat、alone 重複；未發現語言錯誤。

top.comment_zh: 第一段用隔板、布簾、廚師的手、圓桌、生日蛋糕等細節對照，並以 whereas 句歸納；第二段依原因、對個人與人際的正反影響、自己的規則（每週三、日全家不看手機）推進，再延伸到餐廳設計，結尾有見解。句型與用字精準，未發現語言錯誤。
